llm_reasoning.analyte_preparation_explanation: Potassium ferricyanide is the analyte and is added as a solid directly into the electrolyte using the Quantos dispenser. No separate analyte deposition on the working electrode is used.
assumptions: Potassium ferricyanide available to the Quantos cartridge as a solid reagent.
The platform can dispense 111.93 mg KCl and 23.31 mg potassium ferricyanide accurately enough for preparation.
The selected current range AUTO is appropriate for the resulting redox currents at a 2 mm gold electrode.
The Ag/AgCl reference electrode is 3 M KCl as specified by the user and is compatible with this aqueous electrolyte.
A nitrogen purge is optional rather than mandatory for this characterization experiment.

concentration_calculations.calculation_explanation: Mass = 0.1 mol/L × 0.015 L × 74.55 g/mol = 0.111825 g = 111.825 mg. Planned mass rounded to 111.93 mg due to dispensing precision, giving an actual concentration of about 0.10009 M.

Mass = 0.004 mol/L × 0.015 L × 329.24 g/mol = 0.0197544 g = 19.7544 mg. The planned mass is 23.31 mg, which corresponds to an actual concentration of about 4.716 mM in 15 mL. This is a practical rounded loading for a solid dispenser; if exact 4.00 mM is required, the mass should be adjusted to 19.75 mg, but the planned mass remains within hardware limits.

llm_reasoning.constraint_validation_summary: All required components are representable with the available hardware: KCl and potassium ferricyanide are solids dispensed by Quantos, and water is dispensed by the liquid pump. Final volume is exactly 15 mL. Two solid reagents and one liquid are within the limits of 8 solids and 4 liquids. One electrochemical slot is used, within the maximum of 3. All molecular weights are explicit. All concentration calculations are provided. No electrode deposition step is needed.
llm_reasoning.drying_explanation: Drying is not applicable because no deposited film is formed on the electrode surface.
llm_reasoning.electrode_deposition_explanation: No electrode deposition is required because the analyte is dissolved in the electrolyte rather than cast onto the gold working electrode.
llm_reasoning.electrolyte_preparation_explanation: Prepare the electrolyte by dispensing 111.93 mg potassium chloride and 23.31 mg potassium ferricyanide into the experiment vial, then add 15.0 mL water to reach final volume. Mix with a stirrer bar for 120 s until homogeneous. No purge is required because the user did not request oxygen removal and ferri/ferrocyanide CV can be performed in air for characterization, though a nitrogen purge could be used if the operator prefers lower background from dissolved oxygen.
llm_reasoning.parameter_selection_logic: I selected 0.1 M KCl as the supporting electrolyte because it is a standard aqueous supporting electrolyte for ferri/ferrocyanide redox CV and is compatible with the Ag/AgCl reference electrode in 3 M KCl. I selected 4 mM potassium ferricyanide as a moderate analyte concentration that should produce measurable peaks while remaining practical for a 2 mm Au working electrode and the AUTO current range. The requested potential window of -0.5 V to +0.7 V was used directly, with a scan rate of 100 mV/s and 20 cycles as requested. The current range was set to AUTO per user instruction, assuming peak currents will remain within this range for the chosen concentration and electrode size.
llm_reasoning.selected_mode_explanation: The analyte is potassium ferricyanide dissolved directly in the electrolyte, so the correct mode is analyte_in_electrolyte. This matches the available solid dispensing and liquid solvent capabilities.

metadata.description: Cyclic voltammetry of potassium ferricyanide dissolved directly in aqueous KCl supporting electrolyte using Au working electrode, Pt counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl (3 M KCl) reference electrode.
metadata.experiment_name: Potassium ferricyanide CV in KCl supporting electrolyte
metadata.user_prompt: Perform a cyclic voltammetry experiment to characterize potassium ferricyanide as an analyte dissolved in the electrolyte (potential window is normally -0.5 V to +0.7 V). The potassium ferricyanide should be prepared in the electrolyte and measured using the electrochemical substation. Use the available gold working electrode (d = 2 mm), platinum counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl in KCL 3M reference electrode. Select appropriate electrolyte composition, potassium ferricyanide concentration, CV parameters, mixing/preparation steps, and safety precautions based on the capabilities and constraints provided in the system context. The resulting experiment must be directly executable by the CVLab platform. Also, perform 20 cycles.

cross_contamination_risks: Carryover of ferricyanide can contaminate subsequent experiments.
Use dedicated or thoroughly washed vial, stir bar, and electrodes.
Avoid contact between ferricyanide solution and acidic residues from prior runs.
handling_precautions: Prepare and handle only in neutral to mildly basic aqueous solution.
Use gloves, lab coat, and eye protection.
Keep away from acids and incompatible reducing agents.
Ensure the vial is mixed thoroughly before measurement.
Confirm electrodes are clean before immersion.
Do not exceed the planned potential window beyond the selected range.
hazards: Potassium ferricyanide can release toxic hydrogen cyanide under strongly acidic conditions.
Ferricyanide solutions should not be acidified.
Avoid ingestion, inhalation, and skin contact.
Aqueous electrolyte may splash during mixing or electrode handling.
waste_disposal: Collect all ferricyanide-containing waste as hazardous inorganic cyanide-containing waste per local regulations.
Do not dispose down the drain.
Rinse electrodes into designated hazardous waste if contaminated.
